question: Select the correct pairs from the following options.
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω), which is the standard unit in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• Resistivity is measured in ohm-metres (Ω·m), representing the resistance of a material of unit length and unit cross-sectional area.
 
• Option 2 correctly pairs resistance with ohms and resistivity with ohm-metres.
 
• The unit of resistance (ohm) is defined as one volt per ampere (V/A).
 
• Resistivity is a fundamental property of materials that affects how they conduct electric current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance:**

 
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of electric current in a conductor.
 
• It is influenced by the material, length, cross-sectional area, and temperature of the conductor.
 
• High resistance materials are used as insulators, while low resistance materials are used as conductors.
 
 
 
• **Resistivity:**
 
 
• Resistivity is an intrinsic property of a material, indicating how much it resists current flow.
 
• It is temperature-dependent and usually increases with rising temperature for conductors.
 
• Materials with low resistivity are good conductors (e.g., metals), while those with high resistivity are insulators (e.g., rubber).
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• This law is fundamental in understanding and calculating electrical circuits.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Knowledge of resistance and resistivity is crucial in designing electrical and electronic circuits.
 
• It helps in selecting appropriate materials for wiring and components to ensure safety and efficiency.
 
• Resistivity measurements are used in material science to characterize and develop new materials.
